title: T1573.002 — Encrypted Channel - Asymmetric Cryptography
subtitle: The animation shows one full asymmetric C2 life cycle: key setup, certificate presentation, key exchange, signed tasking, researcher clustering, intel sharing, SOC detection...

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: Build keys, embed the public half
steps.caption: The attacker generates an RSA keypair on the C2 server. Only the public key is placed inside the implant binary, so no shared secret exists that a reverse engineer could copy. The private key never leaves the attacker's server
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Implant calls home, server shows a certificate
steps.caption: The implant starts a TLS session to the C2 server. The server presents a self-signed certificate with a weak 1024-bit RSA key and a ten-year validity window. The enterprise boundary records the handshake details even though the content stays encrypted
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: A session key is wrapped with the public key
steps.caption: Inside the established TLS 1.3 tunnel, the implant creates its own AES session key for the application layer, wraps it with the server's RSA public key, and sends it across - the ATT&CK-documented pattern (for example Sliver's mutual TLS plus RSA session-key exchange). Only the server's private key can unwrap it. Older TLS 1.2 channels can do this wrap at the protocol level instead. From this moment both sides talk with fast symmetric encryption
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Signed, encrypted tasking
steps.caption: The operator pushes tasks through the encrypted channel and signs each one with the private key. The implant verifies the signature before it runs a task, then returns results over the same session
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.caption: The SIEM raises an alert because an internal workstation talks to a server that uses the hunted certificate hash and a rare JA3S value. The analyst confirms the beacon and pulls endpoint context for the host

steps.title: Block and hunt back in time
steps.caption: The SOC blocks the cluster IPs and the certificate hash at the boundary, isolates the workstation, and hunts the same fingerprint across 90 days of stored logs. The hunt uncovers two earlier, quieter sessions, so the team can measure the full scope
